prompt: Analyze a materially different, sanitized incident supplied by a qualified reviewer. Without model answers, produce an evidence-governed causal analysis, blameless and accountable post-incident review, and verified risk-reduction plan. Do not use the queue-collapse scenario, and do not access evidence beyond your authorization.
deliverables: Impact statement covering journey, population, interval, correctness or durability, business effect, estimation method and uncertainty.
Evidence inventory covering provenance, source and knowledge time, clock quality, transformations, retention, access class, gaps and conflicts.
Paired system-time and knowledge-time timeline using ranges or partial ordering where necessary.
Claim ledger classifying facts, inferences, hypotheses, assumptions, decisions and unknowns with confidence.
Branching causal graph with at least eight supported or explicitly tentative links across trigger, mechanisms, conditions, propagation, barriers, recovery constraints and luck.
Two alternative explanations with discriminating predictions and rejecting evidence.
One counterfactual specifying intervention, held conditions, prediction, falsifier, confounders and external-validity limit.
Human and organizational analysis using local rationality, interface, workload, permissions, incentives, safeguards and due-process boundary.
At least three action records spanning four defense categories, each with risk, owner role, priority, due logic, acceptance, rollback, telemetry, side effects and effectiveness window.
Publication and access review plus a 90-day recurrence, near-miss and cross-system adoption plan.
evidenceRequirements: Sanitized or controlled source references; no secrets, unnecessary personal data or invented evidence.
Traceability from each factual claim and causal arrow to a source or explicit unknown.
Clock offsets and uncertainty retained rather than overwritten.
Reviewer-observed distinction between correlation, mechanism and intervention.
Acceptance and effectiveness states tracked separately.
Independent reviewer challenge, recorded dissent and remediation history.
Delayed reassessment on a second unfamiliar incident.

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines user or operator journey, population, interval, correctness or business effect, method and uncertainty.
Shows provenance, access, clocks, transformations and retained conflicts.
Preserves gaps and states what sources cannot prove.
Separates system and knowledge time, uses normalized ranges and invents no ordering.
Classifies claims with citations, confidence, alternatives and unknowns.
Builds branching mechanisms, conditions and propagation with reviewed arrows.
Explains failed barriers, recovery constraints and luck without calling them root cause.
Defines discriminating predictions, a safe method, confounders and falsifiers.
States how the test environment or comparison differs from the incident.
Uses local rationality, interface, workload, authority and due-process boundary.
Provides layered controls, owners, priority, acceptance, rollback and side effects.
Defines exercise, telemetry, recurrence window and similar-system scope.
Uses clear uncertainty, neutral language and publication or access review.
